summary: The study describes the use of selective area atomic layer deposition (ALD) to deposit ruthenium on SiO2 and HfO2 surfaces using bis-scyclopentadienyldruthenium and oxygen as precursors. The process was applied to create patterned Ru/HfO2/SiO2/Si capacitor stacks, with the effective work function of ALD Ru measured on different dielectrics. The ALD process was carried out in a hot-wall quartz tube reactor at temperatures between 310°C and 350°C, and the growth rate was observed to be approximately 1 Å per cycle. The study also highlights the selectivity of the process using octadecyltrichlorosilane (OTS) monolayers to inhibit film nucleation on certain surfaces.
evidence: ALD Ru was carried out in a home-built hot-wall quartz tube reactor using RuCp2 (bis-scyclopentadienyldruthenium) as a precursor and dry oxygen. Under these conditions, self-limiting growth was observed at temperatures between ,310° and 350 °C corresponding to ,1 Å per deposition cycle. The study also mentions the use of OTS monolayers to inhibit film nucleation, enabling selective area ALD of ruthenium on SiO2 and HfO2 surfaces.
